tagline.text: A limestone bridge and secret caves over an emerald river

children.text: A national park hidden among limestone cliffs and primeval forest along the upper Cadacan River in Basey, Samar. Ride a banca upriver to explore Panhulugan Cave, then paddle a kayak beneath a massive natural stone bridge arched over emerald-green water.
Sohoton Natural Bridge National Park lies deep in the forest of Basey, at the southwestern tip of Samar Island, across the San Juanico Strait from Tacloban in Leyte. Covering about
840ha
of limestone karst, it was first designated a national park in
, and since

it has been managed as part of the much larger Samar Island Natural Park protected area. Inside are roughly 30 caves large and small, underground streams, waterfalls, and a natural stone bridge carved by the river through the limestone.

The similar name is easy to confuse, but this is an entirely different place from Sohoton Cove, the sea lagoon on Bucas Grande Island in Surigao del Norte. Where Sohoton Cove is a coastal destination toured by boat around a jellyfish lake and island lagoons, this Sohoton in Basey is an inland forest-and-river destination where you travel upriver to reach caves and a natural bridge. "Sohoton" means "to pass through" in Waray, an apt description of a landscape defined by narrow cave passages and the space beneath the stone bridge.

The park's history runs deep. Burial traces from the Stone and Iron Ages have been found in the caves, and during the Philippine-American War, Filipino resistance fighters are said to have rolled boulders down onto American soldiers passing along the river below the Panhulugan cliffs. "Panhulugan" means "a place for dropping things." Basey residents call the Cadacan River the "Golden River," for the way its water turns gold at sunset.

Tours are run as community-based tourism by a Basey residents' cooperative, so a guide is mandatory. The activities — walking through caves and paddling a kayak — are light enough for children to join, but some stretches require ducking through narrow passages, so a moderate level of fitness helps. Recommended for travelers who want a quiet nature adventure instead of a crowded tourist spot, and for anyone looking for a day trip from Tacloban.
The highlight of the tour. After exploring the caves, paddle upriver by kayak for about
20 minutes
and the natural bridge appears, a tall limestone arch spanning the river. Passing beneath the arch and looking up is an overwhelming sight.

The park's largest cave, its two big chambers filled with stalactites and stalagmites. Your guide shines a light on formations as they explain — stalagmites that ring like an instrument when tapped, and rocks resembling the Virgin Mary or animals. Small bats live in the ceiling.

blocks.title: Riding a banca up the Cadacan River

children.text: From the visitor center, ride a banca about
3km
up the river. Primeval forest and white limestone cliffs line both banks, and with luck you might spot a kingfisher or monkeys.

blocks.title: A natural pool beneath the bridge

children.text: Around the natural bridge is a wide pool ringed by limestone walls, good for swimming and relaxing. Many travelers rest on a small pebble beach and eat a packed lunch there. On days when the water level is high, follow your guide's instructions.

blocks.title: Panhulugan Cliff and its wartime story

children.text: The white cliff facing the cave entrance is the setting for the legend of resistance fighters dropping boulders on American soldiers. Looking up from the river, you can really feel how high and sheer the cliff is.
On the way back, as the sun dips low, the wider lower reaches of the Cadacan River turn gold. Book a separate late-afternoon extended river cruise to take in this view without hurrying.

blocks.title: Watching banig weaving at Sohob Cave

children.text: Basey is famous for banig, mats woven with patterns from dyed tikog grass. Inside cool, damp Sohob Cave you can watch artisans who've woven banig for generations, and buy one as a souvenir.
A Spanish-era church on a hill in Basey town, overlooking the water where the river meets the sea. A good quick stop before or after your tour.

Visitor center activities generally wrap up by around 5 PM, so it's best to arrive by noon at the latest. During the rainy season, the kayak or cave segments may be canceled depending on the river level, so check with the tourism office the day before whether the park is operating.

1 hour 15 minutes
, and about
50 minutes–1 hour
from Cebu. One-way fares from Manila run about
Going straight from the airport, a chartered taxi or van takes about
1 hour
to Basey. Skipping the city center saves time.
Vans and jeepneys to Basey run frequently from the New Transport Terminal in Abucay, north of Tacloban. The trip crosses the San Juanico Bridge and takes about
45 minutes–1 hour
, for about
The last van back usually leaves around
6 PM
, so if you run late you could be stranded.
There's also a small passenger boat from Tacloban's port to Amandayehan pier in Basey. It takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
and fares are cheap, but the schedule is irregular, so a van is more convenient for travelers.
From Basey town to Wespal, the village with the visitor center, a tricycle or habal-habal (motorbike taxi) takes about
30 minutes
, with a one-way fare of around
. It's convenient to arrange a round-trip charter where the driver waits during your tour.
If you have a large group or luggage, chartering a car for the day from Tacloban (about
) to combine Basey with San Juanico Bridge is also a good option.
The best time is
March–June

, when rain is relatively light and the river runs clear. At this time the Cadacan River is calm and the water around the natural bridge is at its greenest. Samar faces the Pacific and sees frequent rain year-round, and especially from
December–February
, the northeast monsoon can bring heavy downpours that raise the river level sharply, sometimes leading to a temporary park closure.
July–December

often lies in the path of typhoons, so if you're visiting during this period, keep your schedule flexible. The day after rain, the water turns muddy, the natural bridge is less scenic, and cave floors get slippery. In Basey, the Banigan-Kawayan Festival, celebrating banig weaving and bamboo craft, is held around late
September
to mark the feast of the town's patron saint, San Miguel.

Most travelers stay in Tacloban city and visit on a day trip. Tacloban offers plenty of options, from small hotels at about
a night to mid-range hotels at about

. The visitor center at the park entrance has simple lodging (an eco-lodge) where you can spend a night in the forest, but facilities and availability can change, so check with the Basey tourism office in advance.

There are almost no restaurants around the visitor center, so it's best to bring a packed lunch and water from Tacloban or Basey town. If you request in advance, a simple meal can sometimes be prepared locally. In Basey and Tacloban, you can try binagol, a Leyte–Samar specialty of taro and coconut, moron, a sticky-rice chocolate roll, and grilled fish and kinilaw from the river and sea.

Stop by the tourism office at Basey's municipal hall first to register and confirm fees and whether the park is operating that day. Sometimes you can register directly at the visitor center, but the process can change.
Many fees, like the banca and guide, are charged per boat or per group, so going with 4–5 people cuts the per-person cost significantly.
Bring clothes you don't mind getting wet, non-slip sandals or aqua shoes, a towel, and a change of clothes.
Put your phone and camera in a waterproof pouch or dry bag — they'll easily get wet during the kayaking and swimming.
There are almost no ATMs in the park or outside Basey town, so withdraw plenty of cash in Tacloban beforehand.
The caves are dark with uneven floors, so a headlamp is handy. Helmets are provided on-site.
Leaving early in the morning means calmer water and less sun, making the kayaking much easier.
Combining this with the Marabut Rock Islands or San Juanico Bridge lets you pack a full tour of southwestern Samar into a single day.
Mobile signal is weak around the park. Satellite internet arrived at the Wespal visitor center in
May 2026
, but it may not be usable depending on operating conditions, so arrange your return transport and driver contact in advance in Basey town.

After heavy rain, the river level can rise suddenly, creating a risk of strong currents and flooded caves. During the rainy and typhoon season, the park may close without notice, so check the latest updates from the Basey tourism office before you set out.
A guide is mandatory for all activities. Don't enter the caves alone or stray outside the designated areas.
Even the oil from your hands can stop stalactites and stalagmites from growing, so don't touch or break them. Writing on cave walls is punishable by law.
Always wear a life vest in the kayak and banca, and don't go into deep water if you're not a strong swimmer.
Some cave passages are narrow and low, so if you have claustrophobia or back trouble, discuss it with your guide beforehand.
Carry all your trash back out with you, and avoid bringing single-use plastics if possible.
Mosquitoes and insects are common in the forest and along the river, so apply repellent.
